parsed.summary: Two non-existence (breakdown) statements are formalized for ν > 0. On ℝ³ (alternative C), there exist a smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u₀ and a smooth, rapidly decaying force f such that no smooth (v,p) on ℝ³×[0,∞) solves Navier–Stokes with v(t) ∈ L² and uniformly bounded energy. On the torus (alternative D), there exist periodic data for which no smooth, spatially periodic global solution exists. The most important caveat: the periodic theorem quantifies only over natural-number viscosities (`nu : ℕ`), while the paper's Corollary 10.6 is stated for every real ν > 0.

glossary.note: The junk value never matters here, because every field it is applied to is smooth.

In addition, for all m and K there is C with ‖D^m u₀(x)‖ ≤ C(1+|x|)^{-K}

Smooth f, 1-periodic in x for t ≥ 0, with ‖D^m f‖ ≤ C(1+t)^{-K}
For t ≥ 0: ∂_t v + (v·∇)v = νΔv − ∇p + f (one-sided time derivative at t = 0), ∇·v = 0, v(·,0) = u₀, and v and p are C^∞ on ℝⁿ×[0,∞)
glossary.note: Smoothness makes all derivatives genuine, so no junk values arise.

glossary.plain: In addition, v(t) ∈ L² for each t ≥ 0 and sup_t ∫|v|² < ∞
glossary.note: The MemLp field rules out the junk-integral loophole.

glossary.plain: In addition, v(·,t) and p(·,t) are 1-periodic for t ≥ 0
glossary.note: Pressure periodicity follows the Clay errata.

lean_claims.plain: For every real ν > 0 there exist u₀, f: ℝ³ satisfying (4),(5), smooth and divergence-free, such that no (v,p) is a smooth global solution with v(t) ∈ L² and uniformly bounded energy.

For every natural number ν ≥ 1 there exist periodic smooth divergence-free u₀ and a periodic smooth force f, decaying in time, such that no smooth global solution (v,p) has both v and p spatially 1-periodic.

paper_claims.plain: For every ν > 0 there are a force f ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ³×(0,∞)) and a smooth solution on [0,1) with zero initial datum, compact support, bounded L² norm and L^∞ blowup as t↑1. Consequently there is no smooth global solution with bounded energy, which gives alternative (C).
For every ν > 0 there is a smooth force on T³, compactly supported in time, for which there is no global smooth periodic solution with zero initial datum. This gives alternative (D).

coverage.why: This is Fefferman's (C) for every real ν > 0. The detailed blowup structure on [0,1) is not formalized; only the non-existence consequence is.
The Lean theorem covers only ν ∈ ℕ, ν ≥ 1, rather than every real ν > 0.
Only the breakdown consequence is stated in Lean.

flags.explanation: The viscosity is typed `nu : ℕ` and coerced to ℝ. The theorem therefore only asserts breakdown for ν = 1, 2, 3, …, not for every real ν > 0 as the paper and Fefferman's (D) state. This is inconsistent with the ℝ³ version, where `nu : ℝ`.
flags.probe_idea: Restate with `(nu : ℝ) (hnu : nu > 0)` and check that the submitted proof still goes through.

flags.explanation: Requiring the pressure to be periodic adds a condition inside ¬∃. That makes the non-existence claim slightly weaker than the original Fefferman (D), which did not require periodic pressure. It matches the Clay errata, and the paper's own construction has compactly supported pressure.

lint_verdicts.why: Divergence is only applied to smooth fields, so fderiv takes its true value.
The base 1+‖x‖ is ≥ 1, so the real power is positive and the division is genuine.
u₀ is required to be ContDiff ∞, so iteratedFDeriv is genuine.
The subtraction is in ℝ³ (vectors), not ℕ.
velocity_smooth on univ ×ˢ Ici 0 makes the spatial fderiv and the one-sided time derivativeWithin genuine; Ici 0 is unique-diff at every t ≥ 0.
The separate MemLp 2 hypothesis guarantees that ∫‖v‖² is a real integral, not the junk value 0.
